audit_scope: Static code inspection of preserved legacy engines; no archive execution and no prediction run.

findings.detail: The legacy matching query is formed from a target transition A->B and the scoring target is that same transition's B. The reported historical FINAL score is not valid evidence because target B participates in the query signature.
findings.action: Keep original unchanged. Use only the separate leakage-safe evaluator for any future controlled experiment.

findings.detail: Prior audit notes identified null-evaluation bookkeeping that used ALL instead of FINAL. The legacy result must not be relied upon until separately reconstructed.
findings.action: Treat historical scores as unverified and do not reuse them as evidence.

findings.detail: The preserved engine contains an old embedded archive ending at 2026 draw #107; it is not the current canonical archive.
findings.action: Do not use its embedded data for current experiments.

findings.detail: The recipe predictor catches broad exceptions from component generators and continues; this can hide broken hypotheses and produce apparently valid output from only the surviving components.
findings.action: Any reviewed successor should record component failure counts and fail closed when required components fail.

findings.detail: The recipe predictor fills missing selections with low-numbered values when a recipe yields fewer than six candidates, masking insufficient model output.
findings.action: A research evaluator should mark that target as no-prediction/invalid rather than fabricate a complete pick.

findings.detail: The final holdout rows are sorted by their holdout score before the winner and detailed cases are reported. This is not itself target leakage into each per-target prediction, but it makes post-hoc winner presentation easy to misinterpret and does not replace a frozen, untouched final evaluation protocol.
findings.action: Preserve a single frozen final evaluation; do not choose or tune a winner based on final scores.

findings.detail: The preserved source uses fixed historical draw indices for development and holdout, with locked draws described separately. Those boundaries are tied to its embedded 263-draw archive, not the current canonical date-based archive.
findings.action: Do not transplant its old metrics to the current archive. A successor must define splits by actual dates and dynamically isolate the latest target.

findings.detail: The original holdout and shuffle experiments have not been reproduced against the current archive under the current binding rules.
findings.action: Keep historical metrics unverified until a separate, leakage-safe reproduction exists.

next_gate.name: DATE-BASED-LEGACY-REPRODUCTION-DESIGN
requirements: Do not edit preserved legacy source files.
Use the canonical archive only after Data Guard passes.
Keep R54 and R60 regimes separate.
Select candidate settings only on a chronological validation interval.
Freeze settings before a separate final interval.
Never pass target numbers to a predictor or tuning routine.
Run forward walk-forward; label reverse chronology as retrospective stress testing only.
Compare against a random 6-of-60 baseline on identical test dates.
Do not promote A->B->C, A->T, or MOD5->T from OPEN_DEFINITION without explicit user approval.
